title: Lateral entry into B.Tech after diploma
summary: Diploma holders can often join the second year of an engineering degree, saving a year. Admission is through state-level processes.
qualification: A recognised diploma in a related branch, with minimum marks set by the state.
courses: B.Tech / B.E. (lateral entry to second year)

entrance_exams.name: State lateral entry admissions (Maharashtra: through the Directorate of Technical Education)

opportunities: Same jobs as a regular engineering graduate
Better chances for senior technical roles
next_steps: Check your state's lateral entry notification each year.
Compare colleges on fees and placements.

title: Government technical jobs after diploma
summary: Diploma holders can apply for junior engineer and technician posts in central and state departments, railways and public-sector companies.
qualification: A diploma in the matching branch. Age limits apply.
courses: State public works and electricity board posts
next_steps: Read the SSC and railway notifications for your branch.
Prepare the technical subject and general knowledge.

title: Civil services (UPSC)
summary: The UPSC civil services exam selects officers for the IAS, IPS, IFS and other central services. It has three stages: prelims, mains and an interview.
qualification: A bachelor's degree in any stream, with age and attempt limits in the notification.
opportunities: Officer posts in administration, police, foreign service and revenue
next_steps: Read the UPSC notification and syllabus.
Build a daily study routine and keep a backup career plan.
Look at state civil services (like MPSC) alongside.

title: State public service commission exams (Maharashtra: MPSC)
summary: State commissions recruit for state administrative, police, revenue, forest and other services. Maharashtra's MPSC holds its own exams.
qualification: A bachelor's degree for most posts, with age limits as per each notification.
courses: MPSC Group B and Group C posts
opportunities: Police sub-inspector and other state posts
next_steps: Check MPSC's yearly exam schedule.
Prepare in your home-state language and the general syllabus.

title: Banking jobs (IBPS and SBI exams)
summary: Public-sector banks recruit officers (PO) and clerks through national exams. Many private banks also hire graduates.
qualification: A bachelor's degree. Age limits apply.
next_steps: Read the IBPS and SBI notifications.
Practise quantitative aptitude, reasoning and English.

title: Railway jobs
summary: Indian Railways recruits for technical, clerical and non-technical posts at many levels through the railway recruitment boards.
qualification: From 10th or ITI up to graduate level depending on the post. Age limits apply.
next_steps: Follow the railway recruitment board for your region.
Prepare for the written test and any physical or medical standards.

title: Defence officer entries (CDS, AFCAT, technical entry)
summary: Graduates can join the armed forces as officers through the Combined Defence Services exam and the Air Force common admission test, followed by SSB interviews.
qualification: A bachelor's degree. Age limits and subject needs differ by entry.
opportunities: Commissioned officer in Army, Navy or Air Force
next_steps: Read the CDS and AFCAT notifications.
Work on fitness and on the SSB interview skills.

title: MBA / PGDM
summary: A 2-year postgraduate management degree. It leads to management roles in finance, marketing, operations and consulting.
qualification: A bachelor's degree in any stream, with minimum marks as per each institute.
next_steps: Read the CAT and MAH-CET notifications for dates.
Work on aptitude and communication.
Compare institutes on placement outcomes and fees.

title: M.Tech and public-sector jobs through GATE
summary: GATE is an exam for engineering and science graduates. A good score opens M.Tech admissions and some public-sector company recruitment.
qualification: A bachelor's degree in engineering or science. Final-year students can usually apply.
courses: Public sector recruitment through GATE score

entrance_exams.name: GATE (conducted by IITs each year; check the official GATE website for the current year)

opportunities: Higher studies at IITs, NITs and other institutes
next_steps: Look up the official GATE website of the current year for dates and rules.
Choose your paper according to your branch.

title: Master's degrees (M.Sc., M.A., M.Com)
summary: A 2-year postgraduate degree that deepens your subject and opens the way to NET, research and teaching.
qualification: A bachelor's degree in the same or a related subject.
next_steps: Check CUET PG and your target universities' own admission rules.
Plan your NET preparation early if you want to teach.

title: MCA and master's in computer science
summary: A 2-year master's in computers for graduates, leading to advanced software and IT roles.
qualification: A bachelor's degree (BCA, B.Sc. or others, with Maths in some cases).
next_steps: Check state CET and CUET PG notifications.
Strengthen programming and data skills through online courses.

title: Research and lectureship (UGC NET, CSIR NET, PhD)
summary: NET qualifies you for assistant professor posts and research fellowships. A PhD takes you into research, university teaching and scientific careers.
qualification: A master's degree with minimum marks as per the NET notification.
opportunities: Assistant professor in colleges and universities
Research scientist in labs and institutes
next_steps: Read the NET notification and syllabus.
Talk to a professor about a PhD topic and funding.

title: Getting a private-sector job
summary: Private employers hire through campus placements, online job portals and referrals. Skills, projects and internships matter at least as much as marks.
qualification: Depends on the role. Many entry roles need a degree or diploma plus relevant skills.
courses: Short certificate courses for your field
opportunities: Entry-level roles in IT, finance, marketing, operations and many other fields
next_steps: Create a clear CV and an online profile.
Apply for internships while you study.
Use the National Career Service portal to find jobs and training.

title: Digital skills (IT, data, web, design tools)
summary: Short courses that give job-ready skills such as programming, web design, data analysis and digital marketing. Many are free or low cost.
qualification: No fixed qualification for most short courses. Basic computer use and English help.
opportunities: Better chances in any job that uses computers
next_steps: Take a free course on SWAYAM or Skill India Digital.
Build 2-3 small projects and keep them online.
Add your certificates to your CV.

title: Vocational skills and government skill programmes
summary: Short job-oriented courses in trades and services (electrician, retail, healthcare assistant, beauty and wellness, and more) offered through government skill programmes.
qualification: Depends on the course; many accept 8th or 10th pass.
courses: Courses on the Skill India Digital portal
opportunities: Wage jobs in trades and services
Pathway to a diploma or ITI later
next_steps: Find courses and training centres on Skill India Digital.
Ask whether the course gives a recognised certificate.

title: Freelancing (writing, design, video, coding, translation)
summary: Working independently for clients online or locally. It can start part-time and is open to anyone with a skill, though income is uncertain at first.
qualification: No fixed qualification, but you need a real skill and a small portfolio.
opportunities: Project-based work from clients in India and abroad
Can grow into your own agency or business
next_steps: Pick one skill and build 3 sample projects.
Learn the basics of invoicing and income tax.
Keep a regular job or study while you start, until income is steady.

title: Starting your own business
summary: Starting a small business, service or startup. Government schemes offer loans, subsidies and registration support for new entrepreneurs.
qualification: No fixed qualification. Some schemes have minimum education or age rules.
opportunities: Self-employment and creating jobs for others
Access to government loan and subsidy schemes
next_steps: Test your idea on a small scale first.
Register your business (Udyam registration is free for small units).
Look at government schemes such as PMEGP, Mudra and Startup India.
